title: C Programming - Getting Started
description: Write, compile and understand your first C programs.

lessons.title: Your first C program
lessons.content:
## Introduction
A C program is a text file that a **compiler** turns into a program your computer can run. Every C program starts running from a function named `main`.

## Syntax
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void) {
    printf("Hello, AVS!\n");
    return 0;
}
```

## How it works
- `#include <stdio.h>` makes `printf` available.
- `int main(void)` is where execution begins.
- `printf` prints text. `\n` moves to a new line.
- `return 0;` tells the operating system the program finished normally.

## Output
```
Hello, AVS!
```

## Common mistakes
- Forgetting the semicolon at the end of a statement.
- Writing `Printf` instead of `printf` (C is case sensitive).
- Forgetting `\n`, so the next output appears on the same line.

lessons.title: Variables and data types
lessons.content:
## Introduction
A **variable** is a named place in memory that stores a value. In C you must tell the compiler the type of every variable.

## Important types
- `int` whole numbers, e.g. `42`
- `float` / `double` decimal numbers, e.g. `3.14`
- `char` a single character, e.g. `'A'`

## Syntax
```c
int age = 19;
float marks = 87.5f;
char grade = 'A';
printf("%d %.1f %c\n", age, marks, grade);
```

## Output
```
19 87.5 A
```

## Common mistakes
- Using the wrong format specifier: `%d` for int, `%f` for float, `%c` for char.
- Using a variable before giving it a value.
